title: How to enlarge cursor on Mac: simple steps for better visibility in macOS 27
metaTitle: How to enlarge cursor on Mac: easy steps
description: Learn how to enlarge cursor on Mac to improve visibility and navigation. Follow these simple steps in macOS 27 settings to adjust your pointer size today.
targetKeyword: how to enlarge cursor on mac
intro: To enlarge the cursor on your Mac, open System Settings, navigate to Accessibility, and select Display. From there, you can easily adjust the pointer size slider to make your cursor larger and more visible.
tldr: Open the Apple menu and choose System Settings.
Go to Accessibility in the sidebar.
Drag the Pointer size slider to increase your cursor size.
Customize outline and fill colors in the same menu for better contrast.

blocks.text: Many users struggle to track the standard cursor on high resolution displays. Increasing the pointer size helps you maintain focus during daily tasks. It reduces eye strain and speeds up target acquisition. Whether you use a trackpad or a mouse, a larger cursor makes it easier to spot your location on a busy screen. This setting is part of the core accessibility features in macOS 27. It works system wide across all your applications.
Follow these steps to change your pointer settings. The process is identical for most modern macOS versions.

items: Click the Apple menu in the top left corner.
Select System Settings from the drop down menu.
Click Accessibility in the left sidebar.
Select Display on the right panel.
Move the Pointer size slider to the right to increase size.

blocks.text: Beyond size, you can also change the colors. This helps if your cursor blends into specific backgrounds. In the same Accessibility menu, look for Pointer outline color and Pointer fill color. You can pick high contrast options. A white outline with a black fill often provides the best visibility against dark mode backgrounds. Experiment with these settings to find what works best for your workflow.

If you do not want a large cursor all the time, use the shake to locate feature. This makes the pointer grow temporarily when you move your mouse quickly. It is a great middle ground for users who prefer a standard cursor but lose it during intense work. You can enable or disable this in the same Pointer menu under Accessibility settings.

Sometimes the cursor disappears entirely. This is often a software glitch or a battery issue. If your cursor vanishes, try a right click to force it to appear. You can also click and drag on the desktop to reveal a selection box. If you use a wireless mouse, check the battery level. A low battery often causes erratic behavior or total loss of tracking. If the problem persists, restart your Mac to clear any temporary system conflicts.

Research shows that larger interface elements improve performance. Users spend less time hunting for the pointer. This is true for all users, not just those with visual impairments. By setting your cursor to a comfortable size, you improve your overall efficiency. Do not be afraid to set it quite large if it helps you work faster.

faq.question: Does changing the cursor size affect all apps?
faq.answer: Yes, this is a system wide setting. It applies to every app, browser, and menu on your Mac.

faq.question: Can I return to the default size?
faq.answer: Yes, simply move the slider back to the far left in the Accessibility settings.

faq.question: Does this work on older macOS versions?
faq.answer: The path is the same for most modern versions. If you are on a very old OS, look for System Preferences instead of System Settings.
